Gagai out to write final chapter in 14-year odyssey
Newcastle veteran Dane Gagai has vowed to finish a journey he started back in 2012 by leading the Knights to their first grand final in 25 years.
The centre moved to the Hunter a fresh-faced 21-year-old back in 2012 and quickly developed into a key figure in the side's charge to the preliminary final the following season.
Gagai didn't realise it would be another 13 years before Newcastle would be back on this stage, the Queensland representative spending a stint at the Rabbitohs along the way.
The Great Dane: Gagai to join 300 club
Now back in a grand final qualifier, the centre has vowed to help the Knights upset Penrith in Sunday's blockbuster at Accor Stadium.
"To be able to get back to this position, not just for the club and us players but for the fans and the town is special," Gagai told NRL.com. "The support since I've been at this club is second to none.
"They were there in the dark times when we had three wooden spoons so it's nice to get back to this stage. We're not looking at stopping here.
"We've got a big challenge ahead of us with the Panthers and we're focusing on getting a job done so we can give the fans something to really be proud about."

The Knights fairytale run from wooden spoon to the final four has taken on even greater importance for Gagai, who will return to Brisbane next year to finish a decorated NRL career with the Broncos.
The centre was a young pup in an experienced Knights squad in 2013, coach Wayne Bennett recruiting a number of veterans in a bid to bring success back to Newcastle.
Premiership winner Danny Buderus was lured home from the Super League to help recreate the club's glory years, while Neville Costigan, Jeremy Smith and Beau Scott all followed Bennett from St George Illawarra to the Knights.
PF: Roosters v Knights (Hls)
The 2013 preliminary final was Buderus' final game of rugby league and the Knights quickly dropped away amid Nathan Tinkler's tumultuous ownership of the club.
While his own career didn't end with a title, Buderus is currently on Justin Holbrook's coaching staff and Gagai said the club legend has passed on plenty of lessons to the playing squad.
"He was all about action and leading through his actions," Gagai said. "I've been fortunate enough to play alongside a lot of great players. I debuted under Darren Lockyer [in Brisbane] and then came here with Bedsy, [Kurt] Gidley, Jeremy Smith.
"There were a lot of great leaders I learned from but Bedsy was among the best. He's one of the nicest blokes you'll meet but he's able to go out there and flick the switch.
"He's the kindest man on Earth off the field, but then when he gets on the field he demands a lot from his players so that was the biggest thing I learned."

Panthers v Knights: Cogger, Garner return; Same 19 for Holbrook
Can the Panthers progress to a sixth grand final in seven years or will Newcastle's fairytale run continue?
After finishing 2025 as wooden spooners, the Knights rose to seventh spot at the end of the regular season and have knocked off the Rabbitohs and Warriors to move into their first preliminary final since 2013.
The Knights' gutsy win in enemy territory at Eden Park last Sunday has given their fans reason to believe that a first premiership since 2001 can become a reality.
To make it to the big dance they will need to get past the greatest team of the modern era who are fresh off a week's rest and hell bent on making amends for last year's preliminary final defeat when Brisbane knocked them out.
The Panthers are the NRL's big-game specialists and they will enter the prelim as warm favourites with Nathan Cleary, Isaah Yeo and Dylan Edwards primed to lead them into another grand final.
The Knights and Panthers have met on 60 occasions since Newcastle entered the competition in 1988 but this will be their first ever finals clash.

items.body_excerpt:
'Thoughts of going home': The sliding doors moment behind Phillips' rise
Boom Panthers rookie Billy Phillips has revealed he nearly walked away from his rugby league dream as he battled home sickness during his first year in Sydney.
The 22-year-old has been dubbed the next Isaah Yeo but his NRL career was nearly over before it even began.
A Lake Cargelligo product who progressed through the Panthers junior pathway before moving to Sydney at the end of 2021 to chase his rugby league dream, Phillips couldn't crack the club's SG Ball side and featured in just one game in his first season.
Billy Phillips Try
Living more than six hours away from his friends and family, the young forward struggled with the adjustment and spent countless hours pondering a return home.
Now as he prepares to play his first preliminary final in Sunday's blockbuster against the Knights at Accor Stadium, Phillips has revealed how close he came to walking away.
"There were definitely thoughts of going back home," Phillips told NRL.com. "The move was hard, I was getting home sick and wasn't sure if this was for me.
"I had a great crew around me. The house parents that I moved in with and the boys I was with all pushed me to keep going. I got to train with the [Panthers development squad] Pearls and got to train with the Jersey Flegg boys the rest of the year.
"That was a good experience and got me ready for the next year. Then the next year I was off and racing."

A rugged youngster who gets through a mountain of work on the football field, Phillips grew up working on his parents' farm in western NSW.
After a number of epic battles in the backyard with his brothers, the forward attended boarding school at Red Bend College in Forbes.
A rugby league nursery that has produced Billy Burns, Josh Miller, Joel Thompson and a host of others, Phillips' time at the school set him on a path to the NRL.
"I was playing for Red Bend and the Western Rams when [Penrith pathways staff] Jim Jones and Sam Jones were out there and scouted me," Phillips said.
"I was in Year 11, they rang me up and asked if I was keen on coming down and seeing what the Panthers are all about. Of course I said yes.
"They used to come out to Orange and pick us all up in a bus. With school it was hard for us to get up on weekdays so we'd get the bus on weekends and train before going back home. There were a few nerves on the bus because we were still young but I wouldn't change anything."
Phillips made his NRL debut in Round 26 last year when coach Ivan Cleary opted to rest the bulk of his squad and he entered the 2026 expecting limited opportunities in the top flight.
Instead, he has played in 22 games this season and developed into a key figure in the Panthers pack.
A hardworking forward with crafty skills, Phillips was often compared to Yeo during his time in the Penrith pathway and it didn't take long for the skipper to see why.
"He's been outstanding for us," Yeo said. "We've seen within our four walls how good he's been, not just going into the middle but helping out on the edge; he defends really well.
"His stints have been really big for us. He's got more confidence as the season has gone on, and his last two pre-seasons have been outstanding. There's real confidence from the group with what he can bring, and he's shown that this season. It's a big game for him, and he'll go out and do his job wonderfully."

Roosters utility Connor Watson is in doubt for the grand final after failing a HIA during the first half of Friday night's win over the Dolphins.
Watson was scrapping for a loose ball on the ground in the 32nd minute and copped an accidental hip to the head from Kulikefu Finefeuiaki.
He was sent for a head injury assessment which he failed and was ruled out for the remainder of the match.
"That was a hard one because it came out as a Category 2 and then he went in to do it [the assessment] and they changed it to a Category 1 after a couple of minutes," coach Trent Robinson said post-match.
"He's in the middle of doing his tests now to see where he's at because he got ruled out of the game so I'd say that's still 'watch this space' on Connor.
"We'll see how the tests go."
The 30-year-old will now enter the concussion protocols and is in danger of missing next Sunday's grand final.
Roosters halfback Sam Walker made his return just three weeks after undergoing syndesmosis surgery and played 68 minutes before being given an early mark.
Walker suffered the injury in Round 26 and missed the Round 27 game against Souths and the two finals clashes against the Panthers and Sharks.
Another gun playmaker on track to line up in a preliminary final is Penrith's Nathan Cleary , who sustained a stress-related bone issue in his foot during the qualifying final win over the Roosters.
"Nathan had a pretty quiet week last week, but the week off was certainly nice for him and a few others," said co-captain Isaah Yeo said.
"I'm confident he'll be ready to go.
"If we had to play last week it would have been pretty sore, and he would have pushed through it, but it's settled down a little bit, so hopefully all systems go."
The Panthers welcome back Luke Garner after he was a late withdrawal from the Roosters game due to a minor groin strain.
Also back on deck is utility Jack Cogger after serving a three-game ban for a careless high tackle.

Penrith skipper Isaah Yeo has urged Panthers fans to turn out in force on Sunday afternoon amid fears his side's supporters will be swamped by the Knights army.
Excitement for Sunday's preliminary final is at fever pitch in the Hunter , with thousands of fans set to descend on Accor Stadium as Justin Holbrook's side looks to continue a fairytale charge to the grand final.
Yeo: We can't wait
Penrith fans have rallied in recent days after NRL data showed 65% of tickets had been purchased by Knights supporters earlier this week.
Postcode data suggests 60% of tickets sold in the past 48 hours have been bought by Panthers fans and Yeo is eager to keep the momentum rolling to ensure Accor Stadium is painted black on Sunday afternoon.
"I want a lot of Penrith supporters there," Yeo said.
"The stadium will be rocking, that's what you want in these games. Players want to play in big games and the atmosphere is a big part of that. We're looking forward to the challenge and the crowd."

The Knights have enjoyed a remarkable rise from the wooden spoon last year to the final four in 2026. Justin Holbrook's side is looking to emulate the 2010 Roosters by making the grand final just 12 months after finishing last on the ladder.
It's been 25 years since Newcastle played in a decider and 13 since their last preliminary final, with many in the current squad not even born when Andrew Johns led the Knights to glory in 2001.
Despite the on-field struggles throughout the past two decades, the region's rabid supporter base has continued to pack out McDonald Jones Stadium on a weekly basis.
Captain's knock: Ponga puts on a show
Given that consistent support, the players are not surprised by how many fans plan on making the trip to Sydney and forward Dylan Lucas said the squad is eager to send them home with a victory.
"Everyone's been mentioning how many Newcastle fans have bought tickets," Lucas said. "It doesn't surprise me, we see them pack out the joint all the time.
"To jump on the bus for two hours, I don't think that fazes them. There's a fair few buses heading down so that would be really cool as a fan. It brings our community together and they'll be having a lot of fun heading down there to watch us. Hopefully we can put on a good performance for them."
Having played in six-straight preliminary finals, and five consecutive grand finals from 2020-2024, the Panthers are used to playing in front of big crowds.
It's a different story for a Knights side packed with a host of young stars receiving their first taste of finals football.

While the season opener at Allegiant Stadium helped lay the platform for this year's rise, last week's trip to Eden Park provided their first taste of a truly hostile finals atmosphere.
The Knights weren't daunted by the prospect of 48,000 screaming Wahs supporters and youngster Lachlan Crouch said they are excited to play in front of more than 55,000 fans on Sunday afternoon.
"If it beats the 48,000 at Eden Park last weekend, it will be the biggest crowd I've played in front of," Crouch said.
"There's going to be quite a buzz around the ground when we run out. It will be quite exciting and hopefully we can give them a lot to cheer about."

Newcastle have taken another step on their giant killing run towards the NRL premiership with a stunning upset of the Warriors in front of a record crowd at Eden Park.
The Knights will now face Penrith in a blockbuster preliminary final at Accor Stadium next Sunday afternoon and Justin Holbrook's men have shown no environment intimidates them.

There was drama from the opening minute, Newcastle almost scoring after Kalyn Ponga sliced straight through the Warriors defensive line.
The hosts opened the scoring through Leka Halasima before Fletcher Sharpe levelled the scores before half-time.
Dom Young put Newcastle on top soon after the break and the Novocastrians defended their way to victory for the remaining 36 minutes.
Halasima set up a grandstand finish when he crossed in the corner but Warriors fullback Taine Tuaupiki was unable to level the scores with his sideline conversion.
There was more drama in the final 10 minutes, the hosts coming close to scoring on multiple occasions and Ponga leaving the field for an HIA after a bone-cruncher from Halasima.
In the end the Knights held firm to secure a famous victory and punch their ticket to the preliminary final.

items.title: Ivan Cleary declares Nathan Cleary fit to take on Knights in prelim final - SMH.com.au
items.snippet: Ivan Cleary declares Nathan Cleary fit to take on Knights in prelim final    SMH.com.au
items.body_excerpt:
Penrith coach Ivan Cleary has declared son and champion halfback Nathan a certain starter for Sunday’s preliminary final against Newcastle.
Nathan Cleary is recovering from a stress-related bone issue in his right kicking foot, an injury he suffered in the qualifying final win against the Roosters.
Nathan Cleary at Panthers training this week. Wolter Peeters
The Panthers co-captain trained without incident on Friday night. The club has attempted to prevent the media this week from obtaining images of Cleary training by plastering tarpaulin around the club’s training base.
“He’s going well, definitely handy to have that week off there. So he’s good,” Ivan Cleary said of Nathan during his pre-game press conference on Saturday.
“He’s done the work, so looking forward to seeing him out there.”
Jack Cole has been named to partner Nathan Cleary in the halves, despite Jack Cogger - named on an extended bench - being available after serving a suspension. Ivan Cleary ruled out the prospect of his son starting off the bench.
Penrith coach Ivan Cleary says son Nathan is fit to take on the Knights in the preliminary final. Audrey Richardson
“No, Nat’s ready to play,” he said. “He’s obviously carrying an injury, but there wouldn’t be many players out there at the moment for any team that aren’t. It’s just that time of year, but we’re super confident that all our players are ready to play.”
Cleary said it was too early to determine whether Nathan would be fit for Australia selection for the season-ending Rugby League World Cup. He added there was a chance the halfback’s foot was fractured, but MRI scans are often inconclusive.
“There’s basically enough on there that there’s something wrong,” he said.
“But to you’ve got to go by what I think is called ‘clinically’ - how does it feel, can you walk, etc. So we’ve basically worked out enough that it’s an injury that could get worse, for sure, so we’re trying to manage it as best we can so he can play so we can get him to play …
“He’ll be ready. Yeah, he’s done a bit of everything. He’s actually living with us at the moment, so I’ve actually seen firsthand how much he’s actually done. It’s crazy, yeah. He has left no stone unturned.”
Sam Walker played through the pain of a syndesmosis injury that required surgery less than a month ago in the Roosters’ preliminary final win against the Dolphins on Friday night.
“This is what the players dream about,” Cleary said. “It’s what they go through all the hard work in pre-season for, and all through the year, to get themselves into this sort of arena. So, they’re all true competitors and they find ways to get out there and perform.”
Cleary paid tribute to the Penrith medical staff who had made a slew of stars available for big games. Fullback Dylan Edwards was nursed through a serious foot injury in the 2021 finals series, while Nathan Cleary and Isaah Yeo (pectoral) have defied the odds to figure in the 2026 play-off campaign.
Isaah Yeo has made a remarkable recovery from a pec injury. Panthers Digital
“The medical team’s amazing,” Cleary said. “Their job is way more than just treating people - there’s a lot of decisions to make, even like reading scans and trying to work out what’s the best course of action.
“It’s not like a normal person where you treat them with the utmost care; you’re sort of trying to throw them out on a footy field as well if you can. It’s pretty cool to see how it all works. We’ve got good chemistry through our staff, and we’ve been together for a fairly long time, so I think that helps as well.”
Cleary said a 25-6 loss to Newcastle at Carrington Park in Bathurst last May - a result that consigned the Panthers to last place at the time - was a pivotal moment.
“Oh, that was awful, that game,” he said.
“That was our turning point last year, because it was sort of the day where we just went, ‘right, this is not good enough. We are what we are, and it’s not very good.’

Jack Cogger’s back from suspension, so he’s included among the bench options, while there’s a reshuffle among the middles. Isaah Yeo returns to the first XIII at loose-forward, with Lindsay Smith switching to prop and Liam Henry moving down to the interchange panel.

There’s no panic changes for Justin Holbrook, as the former St Helens and Titans head coach selects the same 19 that accounted for the Warriors last week.
Dylan Lucas remains in the squad after a short stint in his return at Eden Park, so Holbrook will potentially be looking for a longer spell out of the back-rower against the Panthers.

But the Panthers have been simmering around their 2021-2024 form for much of this year, and if they’re even 90% of that level on Sunday then one has to believe they’ll get the job done and reach a sixth Grand Final in seven years.
Cleary’s return could have a big say in the course of this one, and I love the value in a Panthers win and the star half-back crossing at any time at 4/1.
